stem: A postpartum client develops a new abnormal vital-sign pattern that meets the hospital’s maternal early-warning trigger. Which nursing action best reflects the purpose of the early-warning system?

options.A: Initiate the protocol-defined reassessment and escalation promptly because the trigger is designed to identify possible maternal deterioration before the exact diagnosis is known.
options.B: Use the trigger as proof of one specific diagnosis and begin diagnosis-specific treatment without further assessment.
options.C: Ignore the trigger if the client is postpartum because maternal early-warning systems apply only before delivery.
options.D: Stop performing broader clinical assessment because the warning score replaces bedside nursing judgment once a threshold is met.

rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance describes maternal early-warning systems as a way to recognize physiologic changes or other triggers that may precede serious deterioration and require immediate further action according to protocol. A trigger is not itself a diagnosis; it prompts timely evaluation and escalation while the cause is determined. These systems are relevant to obstetric and postpartum emergencies and complement, rather than replace, clinical assessment. B overinterprets a screening trigger, C incorrectly excludes postpartum deterioration, and D abandons the bedside assessment the system is intended to support.
educational_objective: Use maternal early-warning triggers to recognize possible deterioration and initiate timely protocol-based reassessment and escalation while continuing comprehensive clinical assessment.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
source_document_title: Preparing for Clinical Emergencies in Obstetrics and Gynecology
source_locator: Early Warning Systems in the Inpatient Setting — many emergencies are preceded by instability; triggers mandate further actions by the health care team according to protocol; bedside caregivers should recognize changes indicating an emergency requiring immediate intervention; each setting should define activation criteria
source_claim_supported: Maternal early-warning criteria are screening/escalation tools that identify possible clinical deterioration and trigger timely protocol-based evaluation; they are not stand-alone diagnoses and do not replace bedside assessment.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; recognize changes in condition, activate escalation systems, and coordinate timely evaluation
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — maternal early-warning trigger and escalation
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source definition item into a trigger-response scenario. The final version clarifies the key limitation of early-warning systems: they identify possible deterioration and prompt evaluation/escalation but neither diagnose a single condition nor replace ongoing nursing assessment.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ACOG emergency-preparedness guidance. The early-warning section explicitly treats physiologic changes as triggers for further immediate protocol-based action rather than diagnoses.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A preserves diagnostic uncertainty while requiring prompt escalation. No universal vital-sign threshold is invented because ACOG notes that settings define their own trigger criteria.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it uses the trigger for early recognition and escalation while evaluation continues.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; a warning trigger does not prove one diagnosis.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; serious maternal deterioration can occur postpartum and obstetric emergency systems address that period as well.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; the tool supports rather than replaces bedside clinical assessment and judgment.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A accurately describes both the purpose and limitation of the early-warning trigger.
audit_findings.cueing: All options concern how to interpret and act on the same warning-system result.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is directly aligned because the nurse recognizes deterioration and activates a structured escalation pathway.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked screening-versus-diagnosis distinction, postpartum applicability, institution-specific thresholds, escalation timing, bedside-assessment role, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
